newsitem.title: UK: Northern Rock B/S says "delighted" by draft law.
newsitem.headline: Northern Rock B/S says "delighted" by draft law.

text.p: The Northern Rock Building Society, which plans to convert to bank status and float on the stock exchange next year, said on Wednesday it was "delighted" with a new UK draft Building Societies Bill.
"We are delighted with it," Northern Rock director Adam Applegarth told Reuters. "It's a prefectly reasonable compromise and you can't ask for more than that."

Applegarth said the Northern Rock had asked for a compromise on the new rule that 10 percent of a converted society's shareholders could ask for a special meeting at which a motion could be put to waive a five-year protection from takeover enjoyed by the converted societies.
In its latest draft, the Treasury has inserted a new clause whereby 75 percent of voting shareholders would have to approve such a resolution.
Applegarth said this would stop "carpet baggers taking a converted society over by the back door."
Applegarth said the Northern Rock still thinks it "a bit of a shame" that the new law does not distinguish between hostile and friendly takeovers over which the societies would lose immunity.
"But our strategy isn't based on takeovers," Applegarth said. "We have no intention of doing that so our reaction to that is - so what?"
